reason: The preregistration simultaneously preserves the P12-C2 upstream E14f conditional semantic-repair stack and states that any returned model output consumes a cell. This clarification resolves that wording before any P12-C3 provider call without changing candidate definitions, model, prompt, evaluator, gates, seeds, or factorial estimand.

interpretation.cell_generation_transaction: The frozen E14f transaction consists of the initial common-parent model call plus at most one conditional public semantic-repair call exactly as defined by the pinned E14f implementation.
interpretation.cell_consumption_point: A cell is consumed when that frozen E14f transaction returns its final raw response to the parent parser, or when any post-initial-response failure makes the transaction terminal under this clarification.
interpretation.intermediate_initial_draft: If E14f detects a preregistered public contradiction and invokes its single repair call, the initial draft is an internal transaction intermediate. It is never exposed to candidate selection, scoring, cross-batch inspection, or adaptive control.
interpretation.pre_output_capacity_retry: Capacity/transport retry or cross-run resume is permitted only while no response content has yet been returned for the initial request of that cell.
interpretation.after_initial_response: Once the initial request has returned response content, no cross-run regeneration or replacement is permitted. If the conditional E14f repair call is needed, it may execute once as part of the already-frozen transaction. A transport/capacity failure of that repair call is terminal for the cell and cannot be resumed or regenerated.
interpretation.parse_or_quality_failure: A final transaction response that is unparseable or fails the frozen parent proxy/schema/leakage gate consumes the cell as a task/candidate failure and cannot be replaced.
interpretation.completed_parent: A successfully finalized common parent is checkpointed immediately and may never be regenerated.

capacity_policy_effect: Only provider-capacity collection/retry/checkpoint mechanics change relative to P12-C2. Candidate logic and accepted-parent transformation remain unchanged.
